nodes.description: Without SOHLH1, spermatogonia keep proliferating but do not progress to spermatocytes; SOHLH1 and SOHLH2 normally repress stem-cell maintenance genes such as Gfra1 and induce differentiation genes. This is shown in knockout mice; it has not been examined directly in human testis. GO has no spermatogonial differentiation term: an OLS search of GO for "spermatogonial differentiation" returned only CL:0000015, and searches for "spermatogonial cell" and "spermatogonium" returned GO:0007284 spermatogonial cell division and germline stem-cell division terms, which describe division rather than differentiation. The node is therefore bound to the parent process GO:0007283 spermatogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Sohlh1 is essential for spermatogonial differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Loss of Sohlh1 causes infertility by disrupting spermatogonial differentiation into spermatocytes.

evidence.reference_title: SOHLH1 and SOHLH2 coordinate spermatogonial differentiation.
evidence.snippet: The Sohlh1/Sohlh2 double mutant phenocopies single mutants, i.e., spermatogonia continue to proliferate but do not differentiate properly.

evidence.reference_title: The mutation c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 impairs sperm production in the homozygous but not in the heterozygous condition.
evidence.snippet: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and immunofluorescence (IF) staining showed that the germ cells in the homozygous patient’s testis decreased in number and were disordered, indicating the impaired spermatogenesis.

nodes.description: ICSI with ejaculated sperm led to pregnancies in the homozygous patient's partner and in partners of heterozygous carriers. These are individual uncontrolled outcomes.

evidence.reference_title: The mutation c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 impairs sperm production in the homozygous but not in the heterozygous condition.
evidence.snippet: In our study, ICSI was performed using sperm from SOHLH1-mutated males, and their wives became pregnant and underwent successful deliveries.

evidence.snippet: One patient underwent assisted reproductive treatment through an intracytoplasmic sperm injection and achieved a favorable outcome, resulting in a successful pregnancy.

nodes.description: Primary infertility is the presenting problem in every reported man.

evidence.reference_title: The mutation c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 impairs sperm production in the homozygous but not in the heterozygous condition.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the homozygote of c.346-1G > A mutation was found in an infertile patient with an extremely low sperm count.

nodes.description: Reported in four men heterozygous for c.346-1G>A (two Korean, two Japanese). Whether the heterozygous allele alone causes azoospermia is disputed.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SOHLH1 gene associate with nonobstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: We analyzed whether there were mutations in the SOHLH1 gene in 96 Korean patients with NOA. The sequence analysis discovered three novel variations: one intronic variant (c.346-1G>A)

evidence.reference_title: Next-generation sequencing for patients with non-obstructive azoospermia: implications for significant roles of monogenic/oligogenic mutations.
evidence.snippet: These sequence alterations included a heterozygous splice site mutation in SOHLH1 and a hemizygous missense substitution in TEX11, which have been reported as causes of non-obstructive azoospermia.

nodes.description: SOHLH1, with its partner SOHLH2, binds E-boxes in the Kit promoter and activates Kit transcription in postnatal spermatogonia. KIT signalling drives the differentiating spermatogonial stages.

evidence.reference_title: SOHLH1 and SOHLH2 control Kit expression during postnatal male germ cell development.
evidence.snippet: In the male, deletion of each factor causes loss of Kit-expressing spermatogonia in the prepuberal testis.

evidence.reference_title: SOHLH1 and SOHLH2 control Kit expression during postnatal male germ cell development.
evidence.snippet: We found that E-box sequences within the Kit promoter and its first intron can be transactivated in transfection experiments overexpressing Sohlh1 or Sohlh2.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SOHLH1 gene associate with nonobstructive azoospermia.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that a splice-acceptor site mutation that probably causes a nonfunctional SOHLH1 protein results in nonobstructive azoospermia by the lack of normal spermatogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: The mutation c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 impairs sperm production in the homozygous but not in the heterozygous condition.
evidence.snippet: Remarkably, a homozygous mutation of SOHLH1 c.346-1G > A was first unveiled, which disrupts sperm production.

nodes.description: The c.346-1G>A splice-acceptor variant activates a cryptic acceptor in exon 4 and produces SOHLH1 with a truncated bHLH domain. In the homozygous patient, SOHLH1 protein was reduced in testicular tissue. The molecular function bound here is SOHLH1's GO annotation (GO:0000981, ISA, GO_REF:0000113 in QuickGO for UniProt Q5JUK2); loss of transcription-factor activity was shown as failed KIT-promoter activation in transfected cells, not measured in patients.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of transcripts from minigenes carrying the c.346-1G>A revealed that splicing site variation leads to the partial deletion at a cryptic splicing site within exon 4. This deletion results in SOHLH1 with a truncated bHLH domain.

evidence.reference_title: The mutation c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 impairs sperm production in the homozygous but not in the heterozygous condition.
evidence.snippet: Intriguingly, a homozygous mutation of c.346-1G > A in SOHLH1 was detected in a severe oligozoospermia (SOZ) patient, characterized with severely decreased sperm count.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical phenotype and genetic analysis of patients with severe oligoasthenospermia carrying heterozygous SOHLH1 c.346-1G>A mutation.
evidence.snippet: the sperm concentrations for Patients A and B were 3.1 × 10 6 mL−1 and 0.8 × 10 6 mL−1, respectively, with total sperm counts of 9.8 million and 5.3 million per specimen.

nodes.description: Null males are infertile because spermatogonia fail to differentiate into spermatocytes; null females lose oocytes. Seven-day-old null testes lack Lhx8 and have reduced Ngn3 expression.
